messages:
raj: Heads-up — planning to flip prod snapshot buckets from SSE-S3 (AES256) to SSE-KMS using a dedicated CMK (alias/redwood/prod/snapshots). Goal: enforce tenant-level encryption and have KMS audit logs. Thinking next Friday night window.
olivia: +1 for KMS, but we need to validate restore path. Which principal will get decrypt grants? backup-service? restore-runner?
raj: backup-service (IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/backup-service-prod) will keep encrypt permission. For restores we plan to grant the ops/restore role on-demand via KMS grants. Question: should we pre-grant or use ephemeral grants created by restore lambda?
kevin: prefer ephemeral grants created during restore (create-grant + retire-grant) to reduce standing privileges. Also we must consider key-rotation implications — rotated CMK still decrypts old data if using key/material from same key id, but we need to test.
ashley: two operational asks: (1) update bucket policy so only backup-service can PutObject/MultipartUpload, (2) ensure nested backups (snapshots that copy to cold storage) include key metadata.
raj: noted. For RBAC: want to make sure Vault-managed service tokens used by backup-service aren't able to request Decrypt outside expected timeframes. We should tie grants to requestor principal and ip-range. Any objections?
oncall-alex: oncall: if a restore fails with AccessDenied, runbook should include: check kms:Decrypt on key grants, check CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt events, check if grant exists and not retired. Also include aws kms list-grants --key-id <id> output snippet.
sec-bot: automated scan: existing prod snapshots (last 90d) show ~420 objects uploaded without kms:KeyId metadata — these are SSE-S3. Marking for migration and runbook.
olivia: migration plan suggestion: two-phase: (A) stop new uploads to SSE-S3 by enabling PutObject enforcement (bucket policy), (B) run server-side re-encrypt copy using backup-service: aws s3 cp s3://prod-snapshots/<obj> s3://prod-snapshots/<obj> --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01 --storage-class STANDARD_IA (scripted, rate-limited).
kevin: add caution — ensure object versioning and checksum preservation. Also test restore of a re-encrypted object to a test account and verify aws s3 cp into a temp instance with role that has decrypt grant.
ashley: integration with audit: CloudTrail must log kms:Decrypt. We should add an evaluation alert: if restore attempts exceed threshold without corresponding kms:Decrypt events, paging to eng-security.
raj: question on key rotation: if we rotate CMK annually, do we need to re-encrypt existing objects? from KMS docs, rotation doesn't re-encrypt; it keeps backing key material. But still want to validate recoverability post-rotation. Schedule a smoke test after rotation.
oncall-alex: suggested smoke test steps: 1) pick sample object ID 2) attempt s3 cp with a role that uses ephemeral grant flow 3) if AccessDenied, capture kms list-grants and CloudTrail event and escalate. Put these steps in oncall playbook.
sec-bot: reminder: add KMS key policy change detectors to CI so any policy update triggers a PR review and sec-owner approval.
olivia: one more: snapshot export to Glacier must preserve Encryption header. Make sure lifecycle copy keeps SSE-KMS metadata; our S3 Batch operations job should use REPLACE metadata directive.
kevin: I'll draft a minimal runbook + terraform snippet for the bucket policy and a sample lambda that creates temporary grants for restore-runner.
raj: thanks. Action items: kevin draft terraform + grant-lambda (due Wed), olivia write migration script + rate limits, ashley update oncall playbook, alex add smoke test steps. I'll schedule the Friday night window only after sign-offs. :lock:
